subject.title: Auto-update can leave running gateway with stale hashed bundle imports

question: Which availability contract should OpenClaw adopt for stale own-dist imports after an update: strengthen managed generation retention and handoff only, add a bounded one-shot stale-chunk recovery restart, or prioritize the external-updater design?
rationale: OpenClaw controls managed swaps but cannot prevent raw or manual filesystem changes; choosing whether the running gateway should self-restart on a narrowly recognized failure is a user-visible availability and failure-semantics decision.

options.title: Strengthen managed handoff and retention
options.body: Require managed updates to retain the prior generation until the old gateway and tracked work exit, while surfacing a clear restart-required state for uncoordinated rotations.

options.title: Add bounded stale-chunk recovery
options.body: Recognize only verified hashed sibling imports from OpenClaw-owned dist roots and perform one controlled restart before failing closed with diagnostics.

options.title: Prioritize an external updater
options.body: Advance the broader updater process proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77511 so replacement code executes outside the package tree being replaced.

recommendation.title: Strengthen managed handoff and retention
recommendation.body: Require managed updates to retain the prior generation until the old gateway and tracked work exit, while surfacing a clear restart-required state for uncoordinated rotations.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to vincentkoc and the decision spans the gateway/update lifecycle boundary.
